description:
Goal
Apply the same methodology used for the quicksort/operator-sugar non-convergence fix to fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz, which currently still takes roughly 0.8s and exhibits the same class of excess semantic job churn. The outcome should be an upstream data-model fix or a precise proof that an existing upstream fix already covers it; do not optimize native/codegen or transport symptoms until the earliest incorrect semantic/type fact is identified.

Method
- Run the fixture with --log-telemetry before changing code and reduce the log to the first moving facts, not just the hottest downstream job. Track AnalyzeActivation, ActivationInputs, ReturnType, CallSiteSummary, activation key creation, and any transport/native symptoms only as consumers.
- Identify the earliest point where the data model is wrong: evidence descending, equivalent Ty representatives dirtying revisions, recursive keys splitting equivalent list/tuple/callable surfaces, or callsite summaries preserving decisions that should have been joined upstream.
- Ensure decisions flow downhill. If semantic/type/keying owns the decision, fix it there; artifact, transport, native, and codegen must consume settled facts rather than reconstruct or deduplicate them.
- Add focused tests before or with the fix: one small world/type/semantic regression for the earliest bad model, plus the enum_take_drop_split fixture proof. Prefer telemetry-observed assertions for bounded jobs/revisions where available.
- Update .agent docs with any new invariant. Remove any temporary probes or scaffolding before close.

Starting signal
- Fixture: fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz.
- Current symptom: about 0.8s compile/run path despite being green; suspected same semantic churn class as the fixed quicksort/operator-sugar issue.
- Useful comparison from prior fix: operator_sugar went from ~55k jobs / 15s timeout to 275 jobs after fixing upstream monotone semantic facts.

Checks
- fz2 --log-telemetry run/interp/build for enum_take_drop_split show bounded job counts and no repeated semantic churn.
- Existing enum_take_drop_split behavior/matrix tests remain green.
- cargo test --lib.
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings if code paths touched are warning-sensitive.

Non-goals
- No local performance patch in transport/native/codegen unless telemetry proves that layer owns the earliest incorrect model.
- No fixture-specific special case for Enum.take/drop/split.
title: Apply telemetry-first convergence audit to enum_take_drop_split
